title: Red-teaming standardization
bottleneck: Red-teaming — adversarially probing models for failures — has no agreed standards: no common methodology, no coverage metrics, no way to compare results across labs or know when testing is enough. It's expensive, labor-intensive, and its findings don't generalize; a model red-teamed for one deployment surprises in the next. Regulators can't set requirements around a practice nobody can define.
why_it_blocks: Without standards, red-teaming is theater — impressive reports that don't compose into any assurance about deployment safety. Regulators cannot set requirements around a practice nobody can define, leaving governance without teeth.
current_state: Labs run internal red teams and publish summaries; the Ada Lovelace Institute found the practice non-exhaustive, manipulable, and unstandardized. The Ada Lovelace Institute found the practice non-exhaustive, manipulable, and unstandardized - yet deployment decisions rely on it.
